Connect Carbon-Credit Supply with Buyers and Streamline Trading

Thematic Area: Carbon Market Access & Trading Operations

How might we connect eligible carbon-credit supply with suitable buyers and manage purchases, sales and transfers more efficiently?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants to establish carbon-credit buying, selling and intermediation capabilities. It needs access to suitable counterparties, experienced trading partners and a consistent process for progressing opportunities into completed transactions.

The objective is to build a repeatable commercial process covering buyer qualification, credit-offer comparison, quotations, contracts and transaction tracking. Relevant startups work in carbon marketplaces, business-to-business sales software, transaction workflows and secure document sharing.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Missed commercial opportunities: Disconnected buyers and credit suppliers make suitable trading opportunities harder to pursue.
  • Slower transactions: Repeated document requests, fragmented approvals and unclear responsibilities lengthen the path to agreement.
  • Greater execution risk: Complete records of credit status, ownership and transfer responsibilities are essential to reliable transaction execution.

Existing Efforts

  • Available capabilities: Business-to-business sales tools organise buyer prospects, preferences and follow-up. Configurable portals manage quotations, contracts and approvals, while secure data rooms support controlled sharing of credit certificates, registry references and commercial documents. A university decision-support technology offers a basis for comparing screened offers against agreed criteria.
  • Collaboration focus: Develop a commercial model with an experienced trading or intermediary partner. Adapt the transaction workflow for carbon credits and assign responsibilities for credit checks, payments, transfers and retirement.

Potential Market Size

  • Global voluntary transactions: Respondent-reported voluntary carbon-market transactions totalled 84.4 million tCO₂e worth US$535.1 million in 2024. Transaction value fell 29% from 2023, reflecting an active, selective market.
  • Indonesian exchange activity: IDXCarbon recorded 166,476 tCO₂e traded for IDR6.97 billion during January–September 2026, with 160 participants at September’s end.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
